entries.text: For trade contractors who price their own jobs: a spreadsheet kit that works out labour, materials and overhead, then sets the price from the margin you want.
entries.note: Describes the product as the blueprint specifies it; G2 must check it against the delivered file before it ships.

entries.text: A 30% markup sounds safe until you see it is only about a 23% margin. Overhead that never gets spread over billable hours turns small jobs into losses, old material prices go stale, and the estimating still eats your evenings.
Before the quote goes out, you can see what the job really earns. After it is done, the estimate-versus-actual tab shows where you were off, and the price book is better for the next one.
entries.note: No promise of winning jobs or earning more; describes what the kit shows.

entries.text: Enter your costs and the margin you want; the calculator gives the price and shows the matching markup next to it, so you never confuse the two.
entries.note: Check against the live calculator's actual inputs before shipping.

entries.text: Works out a year of overhead per billable hour, prices labour and materials from your own price book, and prints a client-ready quote. Includes a complete worked example so it is useful in 10 minutes.
entries.note: Describes the product as the blueprint specifies it; G2 must check it against the delivered file before it ships.

entries.text: Free templates are a fine start, and ours is free on this site. The kit adds what a blank template leaves to you: overhead recovery, pricing by target margin, a price book and an estimate-versus-actual tab.
entries.note: Describes the product as the blueprint specifies it; G2 must check it against the delivered file before it ships.

entries.text: If you want scheduling, invoicing and a client portal, an app like those may suit you better. The kit is a one-time spreadsheet you own, focused only on getting the price right.
entries.note: Makes no claim about the apps' features or prices beyond the cited claim.

entries.text: The price book is yours: you enter your own unit costs and labour rates, so it fits your trade rather than a generic list. The worked example is a deck; change the lines to match your jobs.

entries.text: Open the kit and fill in the overhead tab first: a year of overhead and your yearly billable hours give your true hourly cost, which every estimate uses.

entries.text: The kit does the arithmetic on the numbers you enter. Check licensing, permit, tax and contract rules for your trade and area yourself.
